data.name: Ai_Intro
data.value: This document describes the full structure of a Power BI dashboard (tables, DAX measures, relationships, and which visual on each page uses which field) so an AI can analyze it and answer questions about its design, model quality or data coverage. **It contains no real data or row values** — only metadata (names, types, formulas, relationships).

data.name: Ai_VisualsHeader
data.value: | Visual | Title | Field type | Table | Field |

data.name: Ai_FiltersIntro
data.value: Filters set at report level (all pages), per page, and per visual. The condition summary is best-effort: for simple categorical filters it shows the included/excluded values; for more complex types (TopN, relative date, advanced) it only shows the type — confirm the exact detail in Power BI Desktop.

data.name: Ai_FilterVisualHeader
data.value: | Page | Visual | Field | Filter type | Condition |

data.name: Ai_Unused
data.value: Objects with no detected use (cleanup candidates)

data.name: Ai_UnusedIntro
data.value: Cross-checking which field each report visual uses, which DAX formula depends on which, which columns back a relationship and which Power Query query feeds which, these objects are not used anywhere. A helper table, parameter or function that feeds a table in use counts as used. Before deleting anything, confirm that no slicer, bookmark or natural-language Q&A uses it either.

data.name: Perf_Bidirectional_Msg
data.value: Cross-filtering in both directions evaluates more propagation paths than necessary and can create filter ambiguity. Confirm that the filter really needs to travel in both directions.

data.name: Perf_ManyToMany_Msg
data.value: Many-to-many relationships are usually more expensive to evaluate than one-to-many — confirm it is intentional and not a modeling mistake (for example, a missing bridge table).

data.name: Perf_CalcColumns_Msg
data.value: {0} calculated columns in this table. Each one takes up space in the model and is recalculated on every refresh — if the calculation can be done in Power Query (M) when loading the data, or as a measure instead of a column, it is usually lighter.

data.name: Perf_NestedCalc_Msg
data.value: {0} levels of nested CALCULATE/CALCULATETABLE. Each level adds a context transition — from 3 on it is worth checking whether it can be simplified with variables (VAR) or less nesting.

data.name: Note_Performance
data.value: Heuristics based on known anti-patterns (bidirectional or many-to-many relationships, calculated columns, nested CALCULATE). This tool never queries real rows, so it cannot measure real cardinality or query time — they are hints to review, not a profiler.

data.name: Note_Usage
data.value: Cross-checks report visuals, DAX dependencies, relationships and dependencies between Power Query queries (a helper table or parameter that feeds a table in use counts as used). It cannot see slicers, bookmarks or Q&A: double-check before deleting.

data.name: Note_Compare
data.value: Compares the model connected now against a .json snapshot exported earlier (the "Export JSON" option) from the same report — meant to audit what changed between one version and another.
